title: The Slinky
hook: A spring meant for ships fell off a shelf and walked, so it became a toy.
peek: In 1943 a naval engineer in Philadelphia was working on springs to steady delicate instruments at sea. One fell off a shelf and kept moving, coil over coil. His wife found it a name in the dictionary.
lede: In 1943, Richard James, a naval engineer at a Philadelphia shipyard, was working with springs meant to steady sensitive instruments on ships. One fell from a shelf and seemed to walk, flipping end over end before settling. He spent the next couple of years finding the right wire and tension to make a spring that would walk down stairs on its own.

bullets.text: His wife, Betty, searched the dictionary for a word and chose 'slinky', meaning sleek and graceful. She later ran the company for decades and kept the toy cheap and simple.
Sales stalled until a Philadelphia department store let the Jameses demonstrate it on a ramp. They sold out their stock of 400 in about 90 minutes.
Hold a Slinky by its top and let go, and the bottom hangs in the air for a moment. It only moves once the collapse, travelling down the coils, reaches it.
The Slinky was made official state toy in 2001, and is still produced in Hollidaysburg, Pennsylvania, where the company moved its factory.
Bubble wrap was meant to be wallpaper and the Slinky was meant for ships. Both found fame doing something else entirely.
The Slinky needed to be seen walking before people wanted one. Post-it notes had the same problem and only sold once people had a pad in their hands.
